steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Mix pumpkin, sweetened condensed milk, and egg yolks in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in 1 teaspoon cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt until well combined.

Beat egg whites in a clean glass or metal bowl until soft peaks form, about 2 minutes. Fold egg whites into pumpkin mixture until no streaks remain. Pour filling into unbaked pie shell and smooth the top.

Bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, combine flour, brown sugar, and 1 teaspoon cinnamon in a small bowl until evenly blended. Cut butter into flour mixture until crumbly, about 2 minutes. Stir in chopped walnuts. Sprinkle topping over pumpkin pie.

Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).Bake pie until center is set and a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, about 40 minutes. Cool pie on a wire rack until room temperature, about 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Brown Family's Favorite Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: This family-favorite pumpkin pie has a rich creamy filling with lots of wonderful spices and a crunchy cinnamon and brown sugar streusel topping.
raw_recipe.name: Brown Family's Favorite Pumpkin Pie

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe for years its the only pumpkin pie my family will eat now! One hint- you dont need to whip the egg whites and it turns out the same, very fluffy and raised. I have always used deep dish pie crusts, makes one very full and nice, I dont use any nuts in the crumb topping.. make sure your butter is very chilled before you start using it, also, add 2 tablespoons more flour, seems to absorb and set better. Lastly, I cover the outside of the crust with foil, it bakes so fast with this recipe, can take it off 10 minutes before its done, but I use frozen crusts, so easier and just as good to me. You really cant mess this pie up, my husband even helps make it, its so easy. ****

This recipe has become my family's favorite Thanksgiving and Christmas staple. It is a different texture, but we like it better than the traditional pumpkin pie. The texture is whipped versus dense. Make sure to use a deep dish pie shell; I add 1 teaspoon vanilla and 1 teaspoon of brandy; make sure to prepare steusel topping before putting pie in oven-there is not enough time to make streusel topping after it goes into oven.

This is the BEST pumpkin pie I've ever had. Super easy to make. I made a few changes but not much. I used fresh pumpkin instead of canned. SO GOOD and makes a big difference. I used 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon and added 1/2 c. brown sugar. I did not separate the eggs (too lazy). I beat them in a bowl w/ a whisk then added the condensed milk, mixed, then added that to the pumpkin. Baked my crust for 6 mins first then filled it. I covered the crust w/ foil after 15 mins to prevent burning. Worked great! This time I chose not to add the topping because I know my husband will not eat it, but I'm sure it would just make this pie even better, if that's even possible. This is a keeper!

BIG hit with the family! Instead of separating the eggs, I just mixed everything together. I also cut out the nutmeg and ginger and added two teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice and an extra teaspoon of cinnamon. I added a 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla as well. Came out perfect! Remember to bake the pie crust before adding the filling for about 10 minutes so the bottom doesn't come out soggy and wrap the crust with foil when baking the pie. LOVED the streusel topping; I made it both with walnuts and pecans and both turned out excellent!

Fantastic! Everyone loved the pie!! Even people who said they normally dont like pumpkin pie, said this was the best they ever had! I took suggestions from others&some of my own... added 1/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 brown sugar and added 1 tsp vanilla, I added 1/2 tsp cinnamon, next time will make it an addtl 1 tsp cinnamon, didnt separate eggs, just put the two eggs in with all the other ingredients and mixed it up! Used only 1/4 tsp salt and I used 1/2 cup pecans and was the perfect amount!
Next time, I'll cut the ginger and nutmeg to only 1/4 tsp each, I like to taste cinnamon more than spices, but thats a preference! I used Pillsbury deep dish frozen pie crust and cooked the night before. let sit for a couple hours then covered and refriged till I took the next day. Left out till after dinner and the pie crust stuck a bit...next time I'll leave refriged till ready to eat. MMMMM... good, wish I had some now to eat! Enjoy!!

Made this pie (finally, it's been in my recipe box for over a year!) for Christmas dinner and party at a good friends house today I really like the flavor. I do like traditional pumpkin pie but this is just a little step above. I'll make this one again but will still like the Libby's recipe for a real basic pie! I did double the spice per one reviewer. I doubled the recipe for two big deep dish pies, so when I doubled the spices, I used "rounded" measuring spoons. That worked fine. I also doubled the topping and used it all but about 1/4 cup. There again, when I doubled the topping, it should have been 4TBS of flour but used 8TBS per another review. Cut very cold butter into the flour/spices. I used pecans rather than walnuts just because I like them better! I did not add the nuts to the topping mixture but sprinkled them on top of the topping mixture after it was divided between the two pies. I had chopped 2 cups of pecans but stopped after putting about 1/2 cup on each pie. Just looked like it was more than enough. Again, great recipe!

This pumpkin pie is amazing! I used a 10 oz (300 mL) can of condensed milk because that is the only size i could find in the store and this came out perfect! and i used pecans because i had an abundance on hand. I did have to bake at 350 for closer to 50 minutes for the pie to set. This was a delicious pumpkin pie! This is definitely our 'go-to' pie for the holidays from now on

Delicious. I used a deep dish frozen crust (it was very full!) and covered the outside crust with foil while cooking, which seemed to keep the edges from burning. I increased the spices (ginger, nutmeg and cinnamon) as others suggested for a slightly spicier pie. I really loved this pie.

I would give this recipe 10 stars if I could. It is so delicious!!! More effortful than a regular pumpkin pie but it's so special that it's worth it. I halved the recipe for the filling to make a standard 9" pie, used my own pie crust recipe, and left the measurements for the topping intact (did not halve them). Even the pumpkin pie haters loved this and my family ate half the pie in one sitting.

Delicious! Made as written using "Butter Flakey" pie crust from this site and I just added the 2 eggs to the pumpkin mix, (I didn't separate/whip them etc. ). Family said better than the usual Libby's pumpkin pie that I make (which is good too).
This is my favorite pumpkin pie recipe. I use fresh pumpkin, baked and pureed, instead of canned.

I've been making this pie for over 15 years now - it's committed to memory. It's a perfect pumpkin pie. I do NOT and have never added the streusel topping though because I like a basic pie and my son is deathly allergic to nuts. Solid pie recipe though!

I LOVE pumpkin pie and wondered if anything could improve on it, but this recipe looked delicious. LOVE it; my wife liked it so much she asked me to bake another the next day for our favorite neighbors. Thirty minutes after giving them the pie, I got a request for the recipe. You will not be disappointed. A great twist on a holiday favorite.
Tastes awesome with or without the struessel topping
Great! I find it makes 1.5 pies... So I double it for 3!
This has been an annual tradition for Thanksgiving and Christmas since my son was born 22 yrs ago!
My husband never ate pumpkin pie until I made it with this recipe. Now he can't wait for Thanksgiving Brown's pumpkin pie!
I've been making this for years now. I'm addicted and I don't even love pie.

Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe. I can't even describe how much the family loved this pie. I fixed it at Thanksgiving and have had requests for it ever since. It's truly exquisite. Update: I just realized I've been making this pie for over 20 years now, as my initial review is from 2002! I failed to mentioned that we used to refer to this as the "holy crap" pie because the first time my husband (who wasn't that excited about pumpkin pie) tried it he yelled from the other room, "Holy crap, this is good pie!!" :)

Everyone is right. This is the single best pumpkin pie recipe ever! I too will be sending my thanks to the Brown family at every Thanksgiving dinner from now on. Thank you for sharing it! Love and hugs to you all.
